title: Haunted La Porte County, Indiana: What's Real and What's Legend (Documentary)
description: A lighthouse keeper who, people say, never left. A former congressman who sat in the dark and heard a drum that, he said, no one was playing. A marker for 499 unknown persons. A country chapel that burned, twice. And in 1905, a newspaper story about a man with no head, flagging down a train.
These are the ghost stories of La Porte County, Indiana, and the true history behind them: what the records show, what's legend, and what no one can prove.

A La Porte Weather Now documentary. Narrated by a computer voice. The photos, postcards, maps, book pages and newspaper pages are real ones, most of them more than a century old. Maps and title cards were drawn for the film.

IF YOU GO
Old Lighthouse Museum, 100 Heisman Harbor Rd., Michigan City: Wed.-Sun., 1-4 p.m. Central, through Oct. 31 (adults $10): https://www.mchistorical.org/visit

Barker Mansion, 631 Washington St., Michigan City: October candlelight tours on Victorian superstitions (6 p.m., $25; dates on its events page). In the museum's words, "This is not a haunted house, paranormal investigation, or ghost tour." https://barkermansion.org/
La Porte County Historical Society Museum, 2405 Indiana Ave., La Porte: https://laportecountyhistory.org/
Kingsbury Fish & Wildlife Area, 5344 S. Hupp Rd.: free and open daily; wear orange in hunting season.

The cemeteries are active and belong to the families: go by day and be respectful. Patton Cemetery was damaged in the Aug. 11, 2026 derecho, so check before you go. Stay off railroad tracks and private land.
SOURCES
Harriet Colfax: the National Park Service; Hoosier State Chronicles; The Keeper's Log (1987); the Michigan City Historical Society
The Barker family: the Barker Mansion and Trinity Episcopal Church markers; newspapers of December 1910
Cathcart's Spirit Room: Charles Cathcart's own account, in Emma Hardinge's Modern American Spiritualism (1870); The Spiritualist Register for 1859; the Indiana Historical Bureau
Posey Chapel: Jasper Packard's History of La Porte County (1876); DePauw University's archives of Indiana Methodism

The headless ghost: the Muncie Evening Press (July 31, 1905, via the Indiana Historical Bureau), the Barbour County Index, the Richmond Planet and the New Haven Morning Journal and Courier (August 1905, from the Library of Congress)
Kingsbury: "Arsenals of Democracy" (about 1941); WKVI; the Towne Post; Places That Were; Indiana DNR
Also: the La Porte Herald-Dispatch (2011, 2020); Lakeland Boating (2026); Find a Grave; the La Porte County Historical Society; the National Weather Service; the Michigan City Public Library
Every source and picture, with links: https://github.com/ScoopAndDude/laporteweathernow-posts/blob/haunts-doc/tools/video/haunts-doc/CREDITS.md

Where sources disagree, the film says so. The 1905 papers call the place Flaherity's Siding, Flaherty's Siding and Flaherty station, on the Lake Erie railway near La Porte. If you know where it was, tell us in the comments.
